title: Herbrand-model consequence is asserted for an unrestricted formula.
details: Fodor, Definite Logic Programs: Models, slide 12 item 3, states that if every Herbrand model of a definite program P models F, then P entails F, without restricting F. Take the language with one constant a and one unary predicate p, P = {p(a)}, and F the sentence asserting p of every element. Every Herbrand model has the singleton ground-term domain and satisfies F. A two-element ordinary model with p true only of the interpretation of a satisfies P and refutes F. Repair: restrict the adopted consequence theorem to ground atoms; every ordinary model induces the same truth values on ground atoms in its associated Herbrand interpretation. The corpus will prove this restricted theorem and its exact term-model bridge.
